messages:
maya: FYI — after yesterday's runtime push (changed kernel selector heuristics + new compile flags) we started getting latency alerts for us-west inference pool. p95 jumped ~110ms -> ~420ms, p99 spikes to 1.2s. Impact mostly long-seq chat payloads (>2048 tokens) on llama-2-13b-quant variants. Anyone digging in? :thinking:

sam: yep, noticed it at 08:12. Trace samples point at attention kernel time, not io. Flamegraph shows attention taking ~70% of token time vs ~20% before. Looks like we hit a fallback to SDPA / generic kernel for some shapes.

irene: attaching trimmed runtime log lines we captured from node inference-07: 

```
2026-03-14T08:10:03Z model=llama-2-13b-quant request_id=tr-8b3 attention_kernel=selected=sdpa reason="selector: seq=2304 batch=1 dtype=fp16" time_ms=112.4
2026-03-14T08:10:03Z model=llama-2-13b-quant request_id=tr-8b3 kernel_launch=attention_kernel elapsed_ms=118.7
2026-03-14T08:10:05Z model=llama-2-13b-quant request_id=tr-8b3 complete total_ms=620.3
```

maya: that `selected=sdpa` is the smoking gun. Prior to the change we were consistently using the optimized FlashAttention kernel for these combos.

ops-bot: Alert: SLO violation p95_us-west > 250ms (rule p95_delta > 2x) triggered 2026-03-14T08:11:00Z.

zach: quick mitigation: we can flip runtime feature flag to force legacy FlashAttention for affected models/regions. I pushed `use_flash_attention=false` in the new selector but it looks inverted — oops. Proposing immediate rollback to previous selector config for us-west (canary 25% -> 100% if good).

sam: another datapoint: kernel_selector.cpp condition looks suspicious. Current logic: `if (seq_len >= 1024 && batch_size <= 8) selectSDPA();` but operator precedence/parentheses may cause unexpected path for batch>1 combos after our refactor. I have a repro patch that corrects the condition. commit: abcdef1 (WIP).

maya: repro steps for ops to validate locally:
1) `export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west`
2) `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"llama-2-13b-quant","prompt":"<long context>","max_tokens":512}'`
3) Observe `total_ms` in response metadata and runtime logs; compare p95 before/after toggle.

Sample curl we used to reproduce:
```
curl -s -X POST https://int-us-west.redwood/api/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-2-13b-quant","prompt":"A... (2300 tokens) ...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Expected: baseline p95 ~110ms token. Observed: ~420ms.

irene: I ran the curl against staging with `REDWOOD_USE_LEGACY_ATTENTION=true` and numbers returned to baseline (p95 ~120ms). So toggling works as a short-term mitigation.

zach: rolling a canary: set `runtime.selector.v=rollback-20260314` on us-west: canary 10% at 08:30, 50% at 08:40, 100% at 08:50 (ops dashboard shows steady p95). Rolling back now -> monitoring.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-selector@us-west -> rollout id r-20260314-02 (initiated by zach).

maya: big thanks. but we need permanent fix: options = (A) patch selector heuristics and recompile (small risk, requires binary rollout), (B) tighten unit/regression tests for kernel selection + add perf regression test (recommended), (C) add runtime metric to detect attention kernel flips per model and auto-fallback to flash if p95 delta > X.

sam: I prefer A+B+C. I opened PR #4823 with the condition fix + a guard that prevents selecting SDPA if `dtype==fp16 && seq_len < 4096 && batch_size <= 4` (bench numbers show flash wins here). Bench results attached in PR.

irene: ops action items taken:
- temporary flag `REDWOOD_ATTENTION_FORCE_FLASH=true` added to us-west config
- rollback-selector completed (deploy-bot reports success)
- increased alert noise threshold while we monitor (p95 delta -> 3x for 1h to avoid flapping)

maya: follow-ups we'll track:
- engineering: land #4823 and run full canary (zach)
- infra: add e2e perf test for seq lengths {512,1024,2048,3072} in nightlies (irene)
- observability: add metric `attention_kernel{name,model,region}` and alert on sudden kernel mix changes (sam)
- runbook: document env var toggles & rollback steps (ops)

zach: FYI the root cause looks like a combo of: changed operator precedence in selector, and new compile flags changed JIT heuristics so kernel-fit heuristics had a different cost model. Both together produced wrong kernel picks for fp16 mid-long sequences.

maya: timeline to hotfix: land selector patch today -> staging canary -> prod patch tomorrow morning. If we see regressions after patch, we'll fallback to forced flash and open a postmortem.

sam: logging note: add trace ids in runtime log lines, e.g., `trace_id=tr-<hex>` so we can correlate trace->kernel selection quickly. PR created: #4826.

irene: I'm updating the incident doc and will create a short postmortem template. Putting links to PRs and deploy ids in the incident doc.

maya: thanks all. If anyone sees any other regions or models impacted, ping here. Closing out once #4823 merges and we confirm stable p95 over 3h. :white_check_mark:
